fixes.what: The 1863-06 gain of West Virginia from confederate-states-of-america adds land the dossier never lost: /ledger/48 (1861-04) takes away only Virginia minus West Virginia.
fixes.why: Territory page (S1), row 20 June 1863: 'The northwestern counties of Virginia, represented by the Restored Government of Virginia in Wheeling ... were admitted as the thirty-fifth state, West Virginia': an admission of loyal counties, not land taken from the Confederacy. The map would outline West Virginia as a new gain in 1863, and the CSA dossier would need a mirror loss of land it never held under this model.
fixes.fix: Delete /ledger/55 and mention the admission in the /ledger/48 note (or in the 1863 keyframe note). If you would rather model Confederate claims, make /ledger/48 all of Virginia and date the regain of the north-western counties to the 1861 western Virginia campaign with a page that dates it; do not keep both readings.

fixes.what: The 1818 Anglo-American Convention land swap is missing from the ledger, though a page the author opened states it and the keyframe 21 and certainty notes cite the 49th parallel line.
fixes.why: Louisiana Purchase page (S5): the northern borders 'were adjusted by the Treaty of 1818 with the British'; 'the territory north of the 49th parallel (including the Milk River and Poplar River watersheds) was ceded to the UK' in exchange for 'parts of the Red River Basin south of 49th parallel'. Territory page (S1), row 30 January 1819: 'The Treaty of 1818 set 49° north as the border with the United Kingdom west of the Lake of the Woods'.
fixes.fix: Add a gain (counterpart british-colonial-empire, region: the Red River of the North basin south of 49N, i.e. eastern North Dakota and north-western Minnesota west of the Lake of the Woods) and a loss (counterpart british-colonial-empire, region: the Milk River and Poplar River watersheds north of 49N in southern Alberta/Saskatchewan), dated 1818-10 (signed 20 October 1818) or 1819-01 (in force, S1), confidence 2, source S5; make sure the /ledger/20 'Louisiana' region and the 1815-1819 and 1820 corrections agree with the new line.

fixes.what: The Japanese conquest of the Philippines is a loss (1942, confidence 1) and its recovery a gain (/ledger/88, 1945), while the existing empire-of-japan dossier records an occupation (occupation_start 1942-05 /ledger/65, occupation_end 1945-09 /ledger/110); Japan's occupations of Guam (1941-12..1944-08, its /ledger/56 and /ledger/72) and of Attu and Kiska (1942-06..1943-05 and 1943-07, its /ledger/66-69) have no US events at all.
fixes.why: Brief rule 3: an occupation of X's land is an occupation in X's ledger; the schema: for occupation_start 'the owner records the same event with the roles reversed'. Timeline page (S2) speaks only of '1944-1946: Temporary reoccupation of the Philippines', i.e. the US was the sovereign throughout.
fixes.fix: Replace /ledger/87 and /ledger/88 with occupation_start (1942-05) and occupation_end (1945) against empire-of-japan for the Philippines, keep the islands as US land in the 1942-1944 corrections (hatched, not removed), and add occupation pairs against empire-of-japan for Guam (1941-12..1944-08) and for Attu and Kiska (1942-06..1943-05/07), each citing a page that dates them (e.g. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aleutian_Islands_campaign, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Guam_(1941), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines_campaign_(1941%E2%80%931942)).

verdicts.summary: Validator clean (0 errors, 5 counterpart-slug warnings, all for listed counterparts_needing_dossiers). 19 spot checks across S1, S2, S5 and S11, weighted to confidence-3 and large-land events: all dates confirmed, no fabrication found, page-silent claims honest except Midway and Wake. Fails on three unapplied blocking findings: the 1863 West Virginia gain double-counts land never lost; the 1818 Anglo-American Convention swap stated on an opened page is missing; the 1942-45 Philippines are a loss/gain against an existing empire-of-japan dossier that records an occupation, and Japan's occupations of Guam and the Aleutians have no US events. No reviewer fixes applied (none was a small verified edit).
